source.basis: Operator facility page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
The published specification for Data Foundry Texas 2 in Austin lists 325,000 square feet of technical space. No IT load figure in megawatts, no power capacity, no redundancy tier, and no cooling specification are published on the operator's facility page as of the retrieval date. Without a power figure, it is not possible to estimate rack count or accelerator density, and any such number would be fabricated rather than derived.

The certifications field is unpublished, so no statement can be made about what workload classes this campus is formally qualified to host. The square footage is large enough to suggest meaningful scale, but square footage alone does not determine AI suitability. Power density per square foot, cooling architecture, and redundancy class are the relevant variables, and none of them are on the record here.

Within Texas, this site maps to a state with 133 tracked facilities, of which only 13 publish a megawatt figure totaling 389 MW across those 13. Data Foundry Texas 2 ranks fourteenth by published megawatts, which in practice means it falls outside the set of 13 that publish any power figure at all. Texas is a substantial data center market by facility count, but the opacity of most operators' published specifications, including this one, makes capacity comparisons unreliable. A reader deciding whether this campus matters to AI should treat the power capacity as unknown until the operator publishes it.
